description: Manually reviewed ground-truth ground-contact frame labels for examples/my_sprint_2.mp4 (right leg), used to validate/reject ground-contact detection approaches for contact_events.py.
methodology: For each of 4 points spread across the clip, reviewed a continuous ~24-frame window (curled-swing -> extended-reach -> curled-swing-again) at high zoom, cropped to the lower body, and estimated the frame where the leg is most extended and the foot is closest to the track surface. This is a best-effort visual estimate, not a precise measurement: motion blur and frame resolution mean individual labels likely carry +/-2-3 frame (40-60ms) uncertainty even before comparing against any detector.

labels.confidence: low - foot stayed low/extended for ~8 consecutive frames without a single sharp minimum, harder to pin an exact frame

comparison_results.note: Distances in frames at 50fps (1 frame = 20ms) from each ground-truth label to the nearest candidate event.

centre_of_mass_y_local_maxima.description: Candidate approach: local maxima in smoothed (5-frame) centre-of-mass y-position, tried as a body-relative alternative to single-limb position/velocity heuristics.
centre_of_mass_y_local_maxima.verdict: Closer in aggregate step count (49 maxima vs ~46 known real steps) than the original detector, but individual-event timing error (100-140ms) is comparable to or larger than real ground-contact duration (60-150ms) - not precise enough to trust contact_time_ms/flight_time/duty_factor.

original_y_peak_detector.description: The existing (pre-fix) contact_events.py detector: local maxima in image-space foot height.
original_y_peak_detector.verdict: Confirmed via direct visual inspection (3 separate samples, see contact_events.py docstring) to sometimes land squarely on the swing-phase peak-flexion moment instead of stance. Error is inconsistent across cycles (-220ms to +40ms) rather than a fixable constant offset, which rules out a simple recalibration fix.

conclusion: Neither approach achieves the precision needed (event error << 60-150ms real contact duration) to trust ground_contact/flight_time/duty_factor output. This dataset is a starting point, not a finished validation set - a real fix likely needs many more labeled cycles (ideally across multiple clips/camera angles, labeled with proper frame-scrubbing tooling rather than static image strips) to either calibrate a more robust heuristic or train a small classifier.
